stories.headline: G7 trade ministers condemn 'economic coercion,' discuss permanent critical minerals secretariat ahead of Évian summit
stories.summary: G7 trade ministers met in Paris on May 5–6 to address critical minerals supply chains, issuing a joint statement condemning economic coercion (widely understood as a reference to China's export restrictions). Separately, G7 nations are in talks to establish a permanent secretariat—potentially housed at the IEA or OECD—to coordinate critical minerals initiatives beyond rotating presidencies, ahead of the leaders' summit in Évian on June 15–17.

stories.headline: Japan's largest anti-war protests in decades challenge Takaichi's military buildup and constitutional revision push
stories.summary: Japan saw its largest anti-war demonstrations in at least a decade on and around May 4–10, with protesters opposing PM Takaichi's arms export liberalization, long-range missile deployments, and calls to revise the pacifist constitution. Takaichi, speaking from Vietnam during the protests, defended periodic constitutional updates as necessary to reflect contemporary security realities.

stories.headline: Takaichi planning South Korea summit visit on May 19–20 to meet President Lee in Andong
stories.summary: Japanese PM Takaichi is reportedly considering a two-day visit to South Korea around May 19–20 for a bilateral summit with President Lee Jae-myung in his hometown of Andong, which would be their third meeting since Takaichi took office. Agenda items are expected to include energy security, supply chain cooperation, and trilateral coordination with the US on North Korea and China.

stories.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent to visit Japan for talks with Takaichi, Ueda on trade and yen
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is scheduled to make a three-day visit to Japan beginning around May 12, meeting separately with PM Takaichi, Finance Minister Katayama, and BOJ Governor Ueda. The visit is part of Bessent's broader Asia trip that also includes Seoul for trade talks before a Trump–Xi summit in Beijing, with currency intervention and bilateral trade expected to be on the agenda.

stories.headline: Japan-China tensions deepen as Beijing maintains pressure campaign and Tokyo weighs labeling China a 'threat'
stories.summary: Multiple outlets reported sustained Japan-China strategic tensions stemming from Takaichi's November 2025 parliamentary remarks on a Taiwan contingency, with China maintaining rare earth export restrictions and tourism clampdowns. Japan's government is reportedly deliberating whether to formally designate China a 'threat' in key security documents, while Taiwan announced consideration of deeper security coordination with Japan on gray zone and cyber issues.

stories.headline: Japan intervenes in forex market to support yen as BOJ Governor Ueda signals continued rate hikes
stories.summary: Japan's government and BOJ apparently intervened in the foreign exchange market to prop up the yen, with Fed custody data suggesting Japan sold US Treasuries in the process. BOJ Governor Ueda separately signaled that rate hikes will continue despite the government nominating two reportedly dovish academics to the BOJ board, with the yen near the 157 level against the dollar.

stories.headline: Quad discussions stall as observers debate whether Japan-Australia-India-US alignment can be revitalized

stories.headline: Japan plans business delegation visit to Russia in late May as post-war economic groundwork begins
stories.summary: Japan's government is reportedly preparing to send a high-level business delegation to Russia in late May (from May 26), including representatives from Mitsui & Co and major shipping companies, to lay groundwork for expanded economic activity after the Ukraine war ends. The move reflects tensions in Japan's Russia policy between alliance obligations and long-standing economic interests.

stories.headline: JSDF fires Type 88 missile in first-ever live exercise with US, Philippines, and Australia in the Philippines
stories.summary: Japan's Self-Defense Forces participated in a multilateral live-fire exercise in Ilocos Norte, Philippines, marking the first-ever overseas firing of the JSDF Type 88 surface-to-ship missile. Defense Minister Koizumi and Philippine Defense Secretary Teodoro observed the launch, which targeted a decommissioned Philippine naval vessel.

stories.headline: LDP publishes immigration policy document outlining new JESTA system and stricter residence rules
stories.summary: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party posted a document on its website detailing policies on foreign nationals, including a new pre-departure immigration screening system called JESTA and stricter enforcement against irregular residents. The document follows immigration emerging as a central issue in Japan's February lower-house election.
